title: Carrots, canned, reduced sodium, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots are cooked carrot pieces packed in a jar with a modest amount of salt and added vegetable fat. The reduced sodium makes them more suitable for people watching their salt intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots are one of the most widely consumed vegetables worldwide and are frequently canned.
Reduced sodium is achieved by lowering added salt and using salt substitutes.
Adding vegetable fat enhances flavor and gives the carrots a richer mouthfeel.
Canned carrots have a long shelf life and do not require refrigeration until opened.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene acts as an antioxidant and supports vision and immune function.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps maintain healthy blood pressure levels.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes regular digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Carrots provide vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Added vegetable fats
items.content: A small amount of fat aids the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin A.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to carrots.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Although the added fat is modest, those monitoring fat intake should account for it.

items.title: Preservative acidity
items.content: Canning liquids may contain a small amount of acetic acid, which can cause discomfort for sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, stews, pasta dishes, or used as a side. Before serving, drain the liquid and optionally rinse the carrots.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.
